newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank Italy should have cautious monetary policy-ABI.
newsitem.headline: Bank Italy should have cautious monetary policy-ABI.

text.p: The Bank of Italy should not rush to reduce interest rates until it becomes clearer if the government will meet key 1997 financial targets, the head of the Italian Banking Association (ABI) said on Wednesday.
"For the markets it's not important if the discount rate comes down tomorrow or the day after," Tancredi Bianchi told a news conference.
He said the important thing was to "consolidate the improvement in public accounts...even if this means a very severe monetary policy from the Bank of Italy".
Bianchi added that a mini-budget might be needed next year if the government was to get the ratio between the public sector deficit and gross domestic product (GDP) down to three percent.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government is currently pushing its 1997 budget through parliament and has said it will push the deficit/GDP ratio to 3.1 percent.
But the International Monetary Fund (IMF) suggested earlier this week that a mini-budget might be needed to meet this financial goal.
"It is hard for rates to fall by themselves without signs of a (mini) budget," Bianchi said. "If the three percent deficit/GDP ratio is credible, the markets will discount a rate cut," he added.

The discount rate stands at 7.5 percent. Bianchi said that if the government could stabilise the net average cost of its debt at 7.0-7.5 percent over the coming months it would be a "notable success".
The latest government target for the cost of its debt in 1996 was pegged to an average 7.7 percent yield on 12-month bills. It saw this falling to 7.0 percent in 1997. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
